    [NormedSpace ℝ E] (g : E → E) (eta eps : ℝ) (y : E)
    {n m : ℕ} {x : E} {r s : E × ℕ}

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let E be any real normed vector space. Fix any function g:E->E, any real eta and epsilon, any anchor y in E, and any starting point x in E. Let n,m be natural numbers and let r,s be pairs in E x N. Suppose
  run(g,eta,epsilon,y,n,x)=some(r),
  run(g,eta,epsilon,y,m,x)=some(s).
Then r=s: both the returned point and the actual reported evaluation count are identical.
The finite exact-real interpreter returns none when its fuel is zero. With positive fuel, it evaluates g(x), sets next=y-eta g(x), and returns (x,1) if ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon. Otherwise it recurses from next with fuel reduced by one, adding one to a successful returned count. The count includes the final successful evaluation. The theorem says that any two successful executions with the same g,eta,epsilon,y,x agree regardless of their possibly different fuel budgets. It imposes no positivity condition on eta or epsilon, no continuity or measurability condition on g, and no inner-product, completeness, finite-dimensionality, or probability-space assumptions. It asserts neither that an execution succeeds nor that n=m; surplus fuel may differ while the successful returned pair agrees.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ApproximateProximalExecution

/-! Deterministic identity of successful Algorithm D.2 executions.
Source: arXiv:2609.06906v1 Appendix D.2, used to join the actual phase kernel,
two-layer center moments and realized query cost. Fuel is an external proof
resource; no success, termination or accuracy is asserted without a run certificate.
-/
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ProximalExecutionIdentity

/-- Two successful runs from the same state/input return the same point and
actual gradient-test count, independently of their supplied sufficient fuel. -/
theorem successful_query_unique {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [NormedSpace ℝ E] (g : E → E) (eta eps : ℝ) (y : E)
    {n m : ℕ} {x : E} {r s : E × ℕ}
    (hr : ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery g eta eps y n x = some r)
    (hs : ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery g eta eps y m x = some s) : r = s := by
  classical
  induction n generalizing m x r s with
  | zero => simp [ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery] at hr
  | succ n ih =>
    cases m with
    | zero => simp [ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery] at hs
    | succ m =>
      rw [ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery] at hr hs
      split_ifs at hr hs with hstop
      · exact Option.some.inj (hr.symm.trans hs)
      · obtain ⟨r', hr', hrr⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.mp hr
        obtain ⟨s', hs', hss⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.mp hs
        have heq := ih hr' hs'
        simpa [← hrr, ← hss] using congrArg (fun z : E × ℕ => (z.1, z.2 + 1)) heq

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ProximalExecutionIdentity

steps.title: Exclude zero fuel
steps.text: Zero fuel returns none, so a supplied successful run cannot have zero fuel. Induct on the first fuel and eliminate zero fuel for the second.
steps.lean: induction n; cases m; simp [proximalQuery] at hr hs

steps.title: Compare identical stopping branches
steps.text: Both positive-fuel runs evaluate the same gradient at the same current x and the same residual test. If that test succeeds, both return the current x with count one. This counts the final gradient evaluation.

steps.title: Compare identical continuing branches
steps.text: If the common residual test fails, both recurse at the same next point y-eta*g(x). Successful Option.map outputs imply successful recursive returned pairs. The induction hypothesis identifies those pairs; applying the same count increment gives equality of the outer returned pairs. No mathematical contraction or termination claim is needed.

lesson.lean_statement: Arbitrary real normed E, g, eta, eps, y, x and finite fuels n,m; successful interpreter equations for both returned pairs imply exact equality r=s. No measure or probability law occurs.
lesson.lean_proof: Induct on the first fuel, eliminate zero successful fuel for either run, then compare the identical residual test. A stopping branch returns the same pair; a continuing branch uses recursive pair equality and the same count increment.
